declaration: int jvs_index_replies(int node, int len, char *reply, char *cmd)

evidence: copies cmd, then the node's automatic command (jvs_frame_command_len[node] bytes), into jvs_last_command[node], so a reply can be matched to the commands sent; checked against reference material (not in this repo); observed live 2026-11-10: in the harness scenario boot (vertical blank 0), called by jvs_bus_setup with node 1, len 0 and cmd 0 right after jvs_query_node had built node 1's automatic command 20 02 02 21 02 (jvs_frame_command_len[1] = 5), it changed the first five bytes of jvs_last_command[1] (jvs_last_command+0x40) from zeros to 20 02 02 21 02; every later call (jvs_read_node, node 1) rewrote the same five bytes; len was 0 in all 963,208 calls, so the copy of cmd ahead of the automatic command did not run

a reply is good when present, ack status 0, sync byte 0xE0, status 1, non-empty and from this node; a missing reply or a bad ack status, status, sync byte or length flags the node (reply_error and report_error), counts jvs_reply_fail_count and the per-node status error tables; a reply from another node (from_node != node) returns 0 with nothing flagged or counted; a good one is copied into jvs_reply_data[node] and indexed (jvs_index_replies), and a failed index sets only report_error and returns 0; checked against reference material (not in this repo); observed live 2026-11-10: called by jvs_read_node with node 1, inf = jvs_nodes[1] and the packet jvs_get_reply had just returned, whose bytes read from node 1, ack status 0, packet length 0x21, sync 0xE0, length 0x1e, status 1, report 1; it returned 1 and called jvs_index_replies with len 28 (length - 2), jvs_reply_data[1] (whose first bytes equal the packet from the report byte on) and jvs_last_command[1] (attract demo, frame 3256)
the checks of jvs_check_reply without the copy and index; checked against reference material (not in this repo)

reads the switch reply (command 0x20, through jvs_reply_offset[node][0x20]) and sets bit 0x10 << player for each player's service switch (bit 0x40), at most 4 players; checked against reference material (not in this repo); declared int but the C has no return statement (as jvs_read_node): no value is returned; observed live 2026-11-10: in the harness scenario test_switch, called by jvs_read_node with node 1, jvs_nodes[1] and service = io_service_buttons: during the six vertical blanks (from 6617) in which the script held the service switch, six calls, and only those of 963,196, took the bit-set path and io_service_buttons read 0x10 (16 << player 0), which frame_io_update handed to coin_input_update as its first argument; every other call stored 0; r0 is a leftover (the C returns no value)

one frame of I/O for a node: takes the reply (jvs_get_reply), checks it, updates coins and service buttons, then queues the node's next command with any extra command (jvs_extra_command) in front; checked against reference material (not in this repo); returns int: its caller frame_io_update calls it through r0 (ghidra/returns.tsv), as for a function declared to return a value, and matches only so; observed live 2026-11-10: called by frame_io_update once per vertical blank (8511, 8512, 8513) with node 1, service = io_service_buttons and the caller's coins array; the packet jvs_get_reply returned was the one passed to jvs_check_reply with jvs_nodes[1], which returned 1, and then jvs_update_coins, jvs_update_service_buttons, jvs_save_command_before and jvs_queue_command (0, 1, 0, jvs_extra_command[1]: no extra command pending) ran in that order

the I/O routine of every vertical blank: does nothing when io_ready_check returns 1; otherwise reads the old I/O or the JVS node(s) (jvs_read_node / jvs_read_two_nodes) and adds the coins read to coins_pending; then, unless coin_input_held is set, takes at most one coin per chute from coins_pending for coin_input_update (the credit service) and drives the coin meters (legacy_io_meters); frame_io_done ends it; checked against reference material (not in this repo); observed live 2026-11-10: called by game_vblank_in once in each of three consecutive vertical blanks (8511, 8512, 8513; two of them inside game frame 3256, so once per video frame, not per game frame); each time io_ready_check returned 0, it read the one JVS node with jvs_read_node (1, io_service_buttons, coins), passed the same coins array to coin_input_update (which returned 0), then called legacy_io_meters and frame_io_done

", the MIE model's text that legacy_io_start had kept) and their end into jvs_nodes[0].id, stored 2, 11, 2, 2, 8 at jvs_nodes +0x94 to +0x98 (players, switches, switch bytes, coin slots, analog channels) over zeros and 0x77 in legacy_io_direction (over the 0x77 already there), and returned 48; legacy_io_poll then served node 0 on every frame
